items.summary: Unrefereed research candidate. A wide binary star takes thousands of years to complete one orbit, so its eccentricity usually cannot be found by following the orbit. Astronomers instead use the angle Γ between the pair's projected separation and projected relative velocity, whose distribution over many binaries depends on the population's eccentricity law. Hwang, Ting and Zakamska (MNRAS 2022, Appendix B) asked whether this angle distribution determines the eccentricity distribution uniquely. In the ideal model (random orbital phase, uniformly random 3D orientation, error-free projections) this package derives the likelihood of one angle in closed form, p(γ|e) = [acosh(1/e) − 1{|cos γ| > e} acosh(|cos γ|/e)] / (π sin²γ), and shows that its mixtures are classical Abel transforms. This gives an explicit inverse for every eccentricity law, including atoms: different eccentricity laws never give the same angle law. The inverse is continuous in the weak topology but discontinuous in total variation, so fine structure can be nearly invisible. Moments need no inversion: E√(1−e²) = (π/2) E sin³Γ and E e² = 1/2 + E cos 2Γ − (1/2) E cos 4Γ; these are the only symmetric unbiased single-angle observables for their targets and give near-efficient power-law index estimators. Two exact selection results bear on Gaia samples: thermal populations keep a uniform angle law under selections that ignore sky position angles, and binning by projected separation preserves the model under a log-uniform semimajor-axis law. The archive contains the 21-page manuscript (PDF and LaTeX source) with complete proofs, a Python library (likelihoods, observables, estimators, Kepler simulators), the full validation script with recorded results and figures, semantic negative controls, fast CI checks, the bounded novelty report and SHA-256 sums. All data are synthetic; no observational catalogue is analysed. items.summary: The magnetotelluric (MT) method uses natural electromagnetic field variations to image subsurface electrical resistivity at depths ranging from tens of metres to hundreds of kilometres. It is widely used in geophysical exploration for natural resources, including minerals, geothermal energy, and groundwater, as well as in the characterisation of sites for CO$_2$ storage and in studies of crustal and lithospheric structure. The MT inverse problem is, however, inherently non-unique: many distinct resistivity models reproduce the observations equally well. Conventional practice nonetheless reports a single regularised model, with no quantitative measure of its uncertainty. MTGeophysics.jl is a Julia package developed to address this limitation. Its principal aim is the quantification of uncertainty in MT model building, advancing interpretation from a single deterministic model, through an ensemble of plausible models, towards the full posterior distribution. The package also provides tools for data analysis, mesh generation, masking, forward modelling, inversion, model analysis and visualisation for MT research and applications. Submission-ready reproducibility release for the PL-Seq reanalysis.

This version includes the revised manuscript source and title, complete Nature-style software references, the bioRxiv PDF build workflow, seven machine-readable supplementary tables, the renamed and updated Supplementary Figure 1 catalog, updated Figure 1 timeline, and stable Zenodo concept-DOI citation metadata.

All repository safety, syntax, and reviewed-figure checksum checks passed before release. This version adds the exact AMD64 Apptainer SIF used for FASTQ alignment, BAM processing, molecule filtering, and PSI reconstruction. The binary environment is accompanied by a SHA-256 checksum, embedded image labels, a command-derived software-version report, and usage documentation. The original Apptainer definition file was not retained; therefore, the archived SIF is the authoritative record of the executed computational environment. This version adds plseq-plotting.sif , a rebuildable Apptainer environment for programmatic PL-Seq and direct-RNA figure generation. It includes Python, Matplotlib, pyGenomeTracks, R plotting packages, Pandoc, and Poppler. The image passed embedded dependency tests, PNG/PDF artifact tests, and end-to-end rendering of the seven-page, 28-gene direct-RNA atlas.

items.summary: The three companions [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] use three structures side by side: probability laws and kernels, provenance (which source a record came from), and differentiation at the boundary of the simplex. This paper studies how they fit together, one layer at a time. Every ingredient of Step 1 is standard in categorical probability; what this step contributes is a set of exact statements about where the ingredients fail to commute, which the later steps build on. The finite distribution monad Dand the provenance comonad W= L×(−) are related by a distributive law λ: WD⇒DW, (l,p) →δ l ⊗p. All four axioms are written out with their types and proved. Its two-sided Kleisli category is the category of Markov kernels indexed by a source, with one source held throughout a composite. Marginalisation is total and affine. Event conditioning is partial and nonlinear. It is undefined exactly where the event has probability zero, it cannot be extended continuously to that wall, and its derivative grows like 1/p(A) near it. Conditioning commutes with marginalisation only for events that are cylinders over the kept coordinates. Contextual Bayes decomposition. Conditioning a pooled law equals pooling the conditioned sources with Bayes-updated weights. In the worked example, source weights 1 3 4 , 4 become 8 15 23 , 23 , and keeping the old weights gives the wrong answer ( 63 160 instead of 9 23 ). Forgetting provenance is marginalisation over the sources. It commutes with every window, but it is not injective: two families of sources can share a pooled law and every pooled table while differing in every labelled table. Step 2, the tangent layer. The cone tangent structure of the tangent companion commutes with the provenance comonad. Each source is a face of the labelled simplex, and a feasible direction leaves that face exactly when it injects whole records under another label; after forgetting provenance, an injected source and a drifting source have the same direction. Marginalisation and conditioning map feasible cones onto feasible cones, with explicit lifts; conditioning’s lift shrinks like p(A) near its wall. The cone T k Hof the half-line is generated by elementary tensors, so it is closed under products, and pooling is a morphism at every order: the pooling paradox lives in the decision functional, not in pooling. Differentiating the contextual Bayes decomposition splits every sensitivity into a reweighting term and a within-source term; in the worked example the answer 9 16 23 moves at rate− 529 per unit of small-trial share. Strata and jumps. The sources that survive conditioning are exactly those with π l p l (A) > 0. Conditioning maps fibres of forgetting onto fibres: it keeps provenance ambiguity on the event, discards it off the event, and can destroy identifiability but never create it. Inside 1 its domain, conditioning moves at rate at most 2/P(A), so nothing jumps and a sudden change needs a rare event. At the wall the limit is the conditional of the path’s leading jet; analytic passages are removable, and jumps need a kink, a non-analytic path, or a jump of the law. Step 3, orders of transitions. On non-negative germs in a Hardy field, order is a semiring homomorphism to (min,+), so every layer operation has an exact order calculus. Each source reaches an event at its own order. The sources of least order survive conditioning, with weights given by leading coefficients; the others vanish at their extinction orders. items.summary: Pre-registered protocol (methods approved 2026-09-29; file sha256 e46e8cc4…) for a fresh-week confirmatory evaluation of frozen methods for inferring IPv6 sibling prefixes of IPv4 prefixes. Published before any evaluation-week data were read. Version 2 adds Amendment 1 (approved 2026-10-02): the published reference of validation week 20260616 is documented as an incomplete build; gates G1/V4 are decided on the three weeks with an intact reference. Published before gate G2 and before any evaluation-week data were read. Version 3 adds the freeze record (2026-10-02): gate G2 passed, reproduction check passed, code hashes frozen. Published before any evaluation-week data were read. Version 4 (2026-10-03) adds the results and the code. It was published after the evaluation: the analysis code; per-query outputs and statistics of all evaluations (E1, E2, E3); the plan, addenda and outputs of the post hoc analyses that followed E3; the completed freeze record (Steps 5–8); and a complete list of deviations and exposures with a map between the names used in the article and those of the code (DEVIATIONS_AND_NAMES.md). The method that the protocol calls the "transfer-aware rule" (code name LX3) is called the "pair-aware rule" in the article. The exposures to evaluation-week information that preceded the protocol (aggregate counts of one archive day, file listings) are stated in the protocol, section E3.0, and in DEVIATIONS_AND_NAMES.md. Not included: reference-pair tables with RIPE Atlas probe identifiers, Prefix Top Lists, and the published sibling-prefix list; README.md explains how to rebuild them. Checksums are in SHA256SUMS. Version 5 (2026-10-03) adds three post hoc items that were run after version 4 under a sixth addendum (posthoc_e3_addendum6_20261003.md): a correction of the ceiling definition, an analysis of Tor pairs that never occur as RIPE Atlas pairs, and the hypotheses without the week of 2026-07-07; their scripts and outputs; the configuration files; an updated list of deviations (items 27 to 29); and a runbook (RUNBOOK.md) with scripts that regenerate the numbers, tables and figures of the article from the released outputs. The result archives of version 4 are unchanged. The published list of validation week 2026-06-16 is called "an incomplete build" in the paragraph on version 2 above and in Amendment 1; that was the name used at the time. What was observed is lower coverage than the list rebuilt from the sources; the cause is not confirmed by OpenINTEL (see the note in DEVIATIONS_AND_NAMES.md, section 6). Version 6 (2026-10-31) adds the reproducibility extension for Sections S8–S11 of the supplement of the article “TRACE6: Tiered Ranking and Persistence-Controlled Evaluation of Probe-Reported IPv4–IPv6 Prefix Associations” (s8-s11-reproducibility-extension-v6.tar.gz), and the plans and amendments of the S8 and S9 analyses as written (protocol_history_s8_s11.tar.gz). It covers the date-matched sibling-list comparison, the overlap-cold analysis and the two-week information window (S8); the re-ranker fold-pool sensitivity (S9); the three-week E4 follow-up of 2026-09-29 to 2026-10-19 (S10); and its post hoc broker-tag strata (S11). All were specified after the E3 results were known and are descriptive. The archive holds plans, code, provenance records, saved outputs and replay commands that recompute every reported S9–S11 interval and mean and regenerate the S8 tables; it does not refit models or rebuild raw inputs. Withheld: the private-storage module of the E4 run controller (see WITHHELD_FILES.md in the archive); no reported number depends on it. README.md and SHA256SUMS are updated; all other files of version 5 are unchanged.

items.summary: Unrefereed research candidate. A wide binary star takes thousands of years to complete one orbit, so its eccentricity usually cannot be found by following the orbit. Astronomers instead use the angle Γ between the pair's projected separation and projected relative velocity, whose distribution over many binaries depends on the population's eccentricity law. Hwang, Ting and Zakamska (MNRAS 2022, Appendix B) asked whether this angle distribution determines the eccentricity distribution uniquely. In the ideal model (random orbital phase, uniformly random 3D orientation, error-free projections) this package derives the likelihood of one angle in closed form, p(γ|e) = [acosh(1/e) − 1{|cos γ| > e} acosh(|cos γ|/e)] / (π sin²γ), and shows that its mixtures are classical Abel transforms. This gives an explicit inverse for every eccentricity law, including atoms: different eccentricity laws never give the same angle law. The inverse is continuous in the weak topology but discontinuous in total variation, so fine structure can be nearly invisible. Moments need no inversion: E√(1−e²) = (π/2) E sin³Γ and E e² = 1/2 + E cos 2Γ − (1/2) E cos 4Γ; these are the only symmetric unbiased single-angle observables for their targets and give near-efficient power-law index estimators. Two exact selection results bear on Gaia samples: thermal populations keep a uniform angle law under selections that ignore sky position angles, and binning by projected separation preserves the model under a log-uniform semimajor-axis law. The archive contains the 21-page manuscript (PDF and LaTeX source) with complete proofs, a Python library (likelihoods, observables, estimators, Kepler simulators), the full validation script with recorded results and figures, semantic negative controls, fast CI checks, the bounded novelty report and SHA-256 sums. All data are synthetic; no observational catalogue is analysed. Assurance boundary: written proofs; floating-point numerical checks and Kepler simulations; producer-side replay in normal and optimised modes; internal AI-assisted review (five roles, adversarial correctness review, proof audit and re-review). This is not peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification. Creator: Anonymous. Prose, manuscript and data CC0-1.0; code MIT.

items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents embedded in software-as-a-service (SaaS) platforms inherit the user's permissions. When a permission is revoked during a task, the platform rejects the next read, but the agent still retains the data it previously retrieved in its context, drafts, saved documents, and memory. This study examined how platforms can enforce a mid-task revocation on that working state. The author defined correct behavior for four revocation types, each mapped to an obligation to block, purge, or suspend, including leaks through paraphrases, aggregates, and existence hints. The author built RevBench, a simulated field-service platform, and compared nine enforcement designs from access control, information-flow control, and machine unlearning on six frontier models in 6,048 runs. Outputs were scored using exact matching and two large-language-model judges. Per-call authorization still failed in 417 of 720 runs (57.9%), rising from 34.4% when the revocation preceded retrieval to 72.8% when it followed delivery. Information-flow labels leaked the least (12.9%) but left revoked data saved in 44.2% of runs. Designs that invalidated the context performed best, while editing the context in place left derived facts behind. A full restart and selective replay with listing-level provenance reached 21.4% and 21.0% substantive failure, the latter with 12.1% fewer model calls. Most remaining failures were disclosures about the restriction, often repeating the platform’s own notice, and larger models did not reduce them. SaaS platforms need revocation controls that reach the agent’s working state and match the type of revocation. items.summary: Unrefereed research candidate. A wide binary star takes thousands of years to complete one orbit, so its eccentricity usually cannot be found by following the orbit. Astronomers instead use the angle Γ between the pair's projected separation and projected relative velocity, whose distribution over many binaries depends on the population's eccentricity law. Hwang, Ting and Zakamska (MNRAS 2022, Appendix B) asked whether this angle distribution determines the eccentricity distribution uniquely. In the ideal model (random orbital phase, uniformly random 3D orientation, error-free projections) this package derives the likelihood of one angle in closed form, p(γ|e) = [acosh(1/e) − 1{|cos γ| > e} acosh(|cos γ|/e)] / (π sin²γ), and shows that its mixtures are classical Abel transforms. This gives an explicit inverse for every eccentricity law, including atoms: different eccentricity laws never give the same angle law. The inverse is continuous in the weak topology but discontinuous in total variation, so fine structure can be nearly invisible. Moments need no inversion: E√(1−e²) = (π/2) E sin³Γ and E e² = 1/2 + E cos 2Γ − (1/2) E cos 4Γ; these are the only symmetric unbiased single-angle observables for their targets and give near-efficient power-law index estimators. Two exact selection results bear on Gaia samples: thermal populations keep a uniform angle law under selections that ignore sky position angles, and binning by projected separation preserves the model under a log-uniform semimajor-axis law. The archive contains the 21-page manuscript (PDF and LaTeX source) with complete proofs, a Python library (likelihoods, observables, estimators, Kepler simulators), the full validation script with recorded results and figures, semantic negative controls, fast CI checks, the bounded novelty report and SHA-256 sums. All data are synthetic; no observational catalogue is analysed. Assurance boundary: written proofs; floating-point numerical checks and Kepler simulations; producer-side replay in normal and optimised modes; internal AI-assisted review (five roles, adversarial correctness review, proof audit and re-review). This is not peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification. Creator: Anonymous. Prose, manuscript and data CC0-1.0; code MIT.

items.summary: A phase-only spatial light modulator in the pupil of a microscope objective can form hundreds to thousands of optical traps at once, but only if the phase pattern it displays is computed well: the pattern fixes how much light reaches the traps, how equal the traps are, where stray light goes, how the pattern survives a real device, and how fast it can be recomputed when traps move. DinHot is an open studio that runs 24 methods (19 published ones and 5 proposed here) on the same task, with the same seeds, metrics and device model, in Python as the reference and in a TypeScript port that runs live in a browser. We describe the optical and device model, the methods with the measured acceptance of each, 14 cases from a 3 x 3 array to a disordered 819-trap array and shaped potentials, the benchmark protocol, two learned models, and the 5 proposed methods, three of which meet their acceptance criteria on their acceptance tasks, each within a scope that the benchmark or the scope measurements narrow (a device-aware weighted Gerchberg-Saxton update, a flicker-bounded phase-continuous sequence and an efficiency-uniformity front), one of which meets a narrowed criterion (an aberration-robust hologram) and one of which is refuted by measurement (a learned warm start for phase-fixed weighted GS). A network trained on three-plane volumes beats its baseline at equal wall-clock on all 162 held-out volumes (median accuracy ratio 1.140), whereas its two-dimensional counterpart ties with Gerchberg-Saxton (ratio 0.9994). The model is a scalar Fourier model of a simulated device, not a calibrated instrument. Interactive studio and reproducible pipeline (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CEFOP_DinHot . Interactive studio: https://dinhot.fasl-work.com .

items.summary: LONG-TERM HABITABILITY OF MORPHING AUTONOMOUS MOBILE HABITATS AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名:可變形移動居住系統長期宜居性極限 56/90 LONG-TERM HABITABILITY OF MORPHING AUTONOMOUS MOBILE HABITATS AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition in the STARLI YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy (Research Institute XXXVI, Flagship 56 of 90). It investigates whether a traceable unoccupied morphing habitat testbed can improve the joint coverage of measured thermal, airflow, moisture, energy and structural engineering envelopes across controlled seasonal sequences while preserving independently reconstructable module identity. Its core coupling is Human-Comfort Proxy Models x Environmental Control x Longitudinal Test Evidence. The project uses guarded coupons, scaled modules, environmental chambers, inert-water and tracer-air circuits, and hardware-in-the-loop tests; it does not observe residents or establish an occupancy certificate. The preregisterable hypothesis is that, under matched materials, energy reserves, maintenance, sensor access, control computation and test time, a frozen morphing environmental-control policy will improve complete-cohort comfort-envelope proxy coverage without worsening module-identity continuity relative to competent static-habitat and expert manual-reconfiguration baselines. The supplied selective-risk candidate R_sel(tau)=E[L(yhat,y)|c>=tau] must be published with accepted coverage, so a low risk score cannot be purchased by refusing nearly every difficult climate or aging case. Hidden trials vary aging gaskets, radiant asymmetry, tracer-air pockets, power outages, sensor common-mode drift, broken connectors, incorrect material identity and ineffective physical stop contacts. Thirty mechanism-specific mathematical plates analyze heat balance, conductive and radiant transfer, operative temperature proxies, vapor mass and dew-point margins, air exchange, ventilation pressure, energy and water closure, sound, light, fatigue, reliability, stale information, uncertainty covariance, selective-risk coverage, tail excursions and second-site reconstruction. Eighty-two chapters contain 410 separately paginated investigations spanning material aging, climate control, indoor-environment proxy limitations, repair, operator authority and versioned evidence. Two hundred Research Gates formulate disconfirmable experimental questions across concealed faults, equal-resource comparisons and two-mechanism interfaces. Thirty-three distinct Phoenix Answer Embryos propose separately falsifiable future rigs, calibration artifacts, safe-stop witnesses and successor evidence packages. The volume is a prospective research design rather than a completed experimental study. An unoccupied thermal or tracer-gas rig cannot establish human comfort, healthy air, habitable water, fire and structural compliance, actual multiyear life, or a right to place people inside a mobile dwelling. The 777-page layout and enumerated items are structurally checked, but a language-duplication audit finds reused long editorial method spans; semantic uniqueness, physical modeling and all evidence inferences remain subject to deeper independent review. Relevant independently identified method references include Fanger (1973), DOI 10.1136/oem.30.4.313; de Dear and Brager (2001), DOI 10.1007/s004840100093; Brager and de Dear (1998), DOI 10.1016/S0378-7788(97)00053-4; Dang, Janssen and Roels (2024), DOI 10.1007/s12273-024-1176-8; Dang et al. (2025), DOI 10.1016/j.buildenv.2025.112867; and Broughton and Maxwell (2023), DOI 10.47120/npl.mgpg103. Standards ISO 7730:2025, ASHRAE 55-2023, and ASHRAE 62.1/62.2-2025 provide bounded normative context, not F56 verification. Author-provided Flagship 13 ancestor DOIs 10.5281/zenodo.23318840 and 10.5281/zenodo.23318839 remain pending independent resolver metadata confirmation. items.summary: Code and results for the paper "Leakage-Aware, Edge-Deployable Brain Tumor MRI Classification: A Latency, Accuracy and Calibration Benchmark". Motivation: Ashwini et al. (doi:10.1155/acis/2622873) note that most current brain tumor segmentation and classification methods rely on offline, static imaging and therefore do not support real-time monitoring. That paper reports results on the Kaggle Brain Tumor MRI dataset (7,023 scans: pituitary, glioma, meningioma and no tumor). This record addresses part of that gap by measuring per-image CPU latency of four classifiers, as a proxy for real-time capability, and by checking whether duplicate images inflate reported accuracy. Contents: a pipeline that audits the dataset for exact and near-duplicate images, builds naive and leakage-aware splits, fine-tunes MobileNetV3, EfficientNet-B0, ResNet50 and Inception-ResNet-v2 over three seeds, measures batch-1 CPU latency, and evaluates calibration. Folders: results (main 24 runs; 7,215 images, duplicate distance 0) and results_laptop (reduced MobileNetV3 runs; 7,200 images, duplicate distance 1). The MRI images are not included; the dataset is on Kaggle (doi:10.34740/KAGGLE/DSV/2645886). See README.md for the run order.
